dana: Ran a 4xA100 nsys+perfetto trace on the kernel-selector regression from last deploy. Seeing repeated collective overlaps during KV cache retire, looks like all-reduce + small kernel storms causing pipeline stalls. attaching initial notes.
jia: can you drop the trace link and the exact cmd you ran? i want to reproduce locally.
dana: link: https://perf.internal/redwood/traces/1719998888 (redwood-internal)

dana: command I used:
```
nsys profile --output=trace_4gpu --trace=nvtx,cuda,nccl --cpuctx=none --force-overwrite --sample=none --duration=auto --capture-range=nvtx -- python -u run_repro.py --batch-size 4 --seq-len 1024
```

matt: thanks. did you capture NCCL traces (nvtx ranges look noisy in perfetto screenshot).
dana: yes, nsys captured NCCL ranges + cuda kernel timings. perfetto shows repeated all-reduce windows (~1.8-2.2ms) that overlap with our short kernels (0.1-0.5ms). timing graph: around t=36.4s the KV retire causes a small kernel burst, which delays enqueueing of the next chunk and extends NCCL window.
leo: could this be our batching heuristic resizing when it sees a short tail? iirc we adjust batch width on tail detection, which could cause more tiny kernels.
dana: exact sequence observed:
- host schedules kv-retire kernel (0.2ms)
- selector launches tiny attention kernels (0.05-0.15ms) x 6
- NCCL all-reduce already started: allreduce spans across the tiny kernels and the larger ones => pipeline bubble
- overall latency for that request + subsequent ones +20-40ms

bench-bot: PERF REPORT: 4-gpu run baseline (pre-regress) median p95 latency 98ms -> current 126ms (+28.6%). CPU/KV retire increased wall time by ~11%.

jia: can you export the perfetto slice IDs for those NVTX markers? i want to map kernel names to ranges.
dana: slice ids: nvtx_slice=0x7f34a (kv-retire), nvtx_slice=0x7f34b (selector:pick_kernels), nvtx_slice=0x7f34c (nccl:allreduce_start). I'll paste perfetto query in a sec.

dana: perfetto query snippet to filter: `cpu_track.name == "nvtx" && slice.name =~ ".*(kv-retire|pick_kernels|allreduce).*"` => shows repeated pattern every 12-16ms.

matt: possible causes: kernel-selection now tries more micro-kernel variants when sequence length jumps -> more enqueues. can we force single-kernel path for the repro and see impact?
leo: also try disabling KV retire prefetcher to see if eviction chatter triggers the selector path.

dana: did a quick A/B:
- forced single-kernel path => p95 down to 104ms
- disabled kv-retire prefetch => p95 110ms
so both help, single-kernel path most impactful.

matt: interesting. that suggests selector branch explosion is the main amplifier. need to look at heuristics that trigger multi-variant selection when queued kernels are already tight.

jia: also run with NCCL_COLLNET=0 and NCCL_DEBUG=WARN to get more verbose collective timing; maybe NCCL is merging operations due to stream ordering.
dana: good call, will run with NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME and NCCL_DEBUG next and post traces.

ci-bot: CI benchmark note: replicated micro-bench harness run scheduled for team/eng-runtime/perf-repro at 2024-07-15T14:30Z.

matt: next actionable steps:
1) dana: re-run with NCCL_DEBUG and perfetto capture of host enqueue times.
2) leo: instrument selector to log variant decision count per request.
3) jia: prepare a reduced test that forces quick sequence length toggles to hit the heuristic.
4) bench-bot: schedule nightly comparison of pre-regress vs head for 4-gpu case.

dana: copying results to the perf doc and will ping when new traces are up. thanks all :thumbsup:
